security.heading: What the policies are
security.body: Friction, not a security boundary. A policy makes a risky action refused, asked about, warned on or flagged — not impossible. Advisory text can be ignored, and a block on the shell can be sidestepped by a determined agent. Each label says exactly how far a policy goes.

security.heading: What the site does
security.body: The site is static files: nothing you pick leaves your machine, and the builder runs in your browser. Your selection lives in the URL fragment after the #, which browsers never send to a server. A policy you draft on the author page is saved only in this browser's localStorage; the page never sends it anywhere, and its share link carries the agent and catalog ids, never your draft. There is no cookie and no account. The site counts page views and a few actions, with no personal data; the list is at the end of this page.

security.heading: Why the command is safe to read before running
security.body: The command fetches one pinned catalog commit and checks every policy against its sha256 — the same hash shown on the policy's page. If the pack does not match, the install fails and nothing is written. The commit must be on a branch or tag the catalog publishes, so a link cannot point at a fork's code.

security.heading: How to report a problem
security.body: Report it as a security issue in the chock-catalog repository, not as a public issue in the engine or the site.

install.install_note: Python 3.11 or newer. The engine is the only install; the plugin is generated from the pinned catalog.
install.run_body: Pick your agent and your policies on the builder, copy the command and run it in your repo. --client names the agent. For an agent marked tested, --apply also runs that agent's own install steps; for an untested agent the command only builds the plugin, and you run the steps yourself.
install.update_body: Change your picks in the builder and re-run the command. Each agent's last step above says how it picks up a rebuild.
install.remove_body: Each agent's section above ends with its remove steps.
install.file_body: A selection is a small JSON or YAML file naming the agent, the pinned catalog commit and the policies you picked. The builder writes one for you; the install command reads the same file. These are the fields it checks:

file_fields.meaning: the agent the plugin is built for: __CLIENTS__. --client on the command line overrides it.
the plugin's version, __BUNDLE_VERSION__ from this site.
the pinned catalog commit; the plugin builds only from it.
optional — a named catalog release over the commit.
optional — the preset the picks started from.
one entry per picked policy: from (catalog), id, version and sha256.

warning_texts.missing_partner: __PRESENT__ is picked without __ABSENT__: the two cover one rule by different means; pick both.
warning_texts.all_present: __PRESENT__ are all picked and overlap: keep one, or the same action is checked twice.
warning_texts.file_absent: __PRESENT__ refuses everything until your repo has __FILE__. Create it before you install.
warning_texts.grade:advise: __PRESENT__ is text only: nothing stops a violation.
warning_texts.missing_partner:many: __PRESENT__ are picked without __ABSENT__: they cover one rule by different means; pick them all.
warning_texts.file_absent:many: __PRESENT__ refuse everything until your repo has __FILE__. Create it before you install.
warning_texts.grade:advise:many: __PRESENT__ are text only: nothing stops a violation.
warning_texts.overlap: chock install warns when a picked policy is already in another chock plugin for the same agent: both copies would fire.
